corrections.reason: Protocol section 4 assigns Grade C to archived, undated, or visibly outdated official material. The cited source records 'Visible date: none is shown' and states in its own notes that 'the document is undated, so its currency cannot be checked, which is why claims resting on it are graded C'. The four sibling claims resting on the same source are all graded C on that stated ground; Grade B here is inconsistent with the source record and with section 4.

Protocol section 9 requires a stated cell to record its claimIds together with its actionable-value note, and the proviso is part of the actionable value because it tells the citizen which applicants the figure covers.

The cell state stays 'stated'; the figure itself still comes from claim_delhi_birth_issue_within_seven_days.

corrections.reason: Protocol section 8 admits a contact route for the owner cell only where it is a contact route for the role that holds or decides the case. claim_delhi_birth_directorate_office_contact gives the Directorate's email and telephone, but claim_delhi_birth_chief_registrar_not_issuer, listed in the same cell, establishes that the Office of Chief Registrar (B&D) does not itself issue birth certificates. The contact therefore routes the citizen to an office that expressly does not hold this case, and does not support the cell's state.
